# The workspace's batch executor (decision 0039). Seeded by stage 00; edit it per site.
#
# Required, not optional in spirit: GARS submits real work to a managed scheduler and never
# runs it in the current process (decision 0027). This file says WHICH scheduler. Delete it
# and the built-in Slurm descriptor below is what you get, byte for byte -- so an existing
# cluster workspace behaves exactly as it always has.
#
# The shape is deliberately narrow -- scalars, one-level lists, one-level `key: value` maps.
# `_system/` is stdlib-only (decision 0011), so this is parsed by a small parser we own, not
# by a YAML library. Do not reach for anchors, multi-line scalars or nested lists.
#
# Three doors, and nothing else:
#   header   the directives block the generated submit.sh opens with
#   submit   the argv that hands that GENERATED script to the scheduler -> a job id
#   status   the argv that asks after it -> PENDING | RUNNING | COMPLETED | FAILED
#
# `submit_argv` runs the generated `submit.sh` and nothing else. It is not a place to add
# pipeline parameters, environment or wrapper logic: the audited parameter surface is
# `_config/<assay>.yaml`, and bypassing it is the one thing this file must never enable.

# The backend. `slurm` and `local` are built in; any other name means this file supplies the
# whole descriptor. (`local` runs the script detached on this machine and reports its PID --
# it is for testing the submit->status walk without a cluster, never a venue for analyses.)
name: slurm

# The directives block. Available placeholders, and only these:
#   {project} {assay} {substage} {partition} {time} {cpus} {mem}
# compute.partition / time / cpus / mem come from `_config/<assay>.yaml`.
directives:
  - "#SBATCH --job-name={project}-{assay}"
  - "#SBATCH --partition={partition}"
  - "#SBATCH --time={time}"
  - "#SBATCH --cpus-per-task={cpus}"
  - "#SBATCH --mem={mem}"
  - "#SBATCH --output={substage}/logs/slurm-%j.out"
  - "#SBATCH --error={substage}/logs/slurm-%j.err"

# How a script becomes a job. {script} is the generated submit.sh; it must appear.
submit_argv:
  - sbatch
  - "{script}"

# How the job id is read back out of what submit printed. First capture group wins.
# A quoted value is taken verbatim -- there is no escape processing, so a regex is
# written exactly as a regex, single backslashes and all.
job_id_regex: "Submitted batch job (\d+)"

# How the job is asked after. {job_id} must appear.
status_argv:
  - sacct
  - -j
  - "{job_id}"
  - --format=State
  - --noheader

# This backend's states, mapped onto the closed vocabulary. Closed means closed: a state that
# is not listed here is refused by name rather than guessed at, so an unfamiliar scheduler
# state can never be silently read as success.
status_map:
  PENDING: PENDING
  CONFIGURING: PENDING
  REQUEUED: PENDING
  SUSPENDED: PENDING
  PREEMPTED: PENDING
  RUNNING: RUNNING
  COMPLETING: RUNNING
  RESIZING: RUNNING
  COMPLETED: COMPLETED
  FAILED: FAILED
  CANCELLED: FAILED
  TIMEOUT: FAILED
  NODE_FAIL: FAILED
  OUT_OF_MEMORY: FAILED
  BOOT_FAIL: FAILED
  DEADLINE: FAILED
  REVOKED: FAILED

# The Nextflow executor config this backend pairs with, under `_config/`. The wrapper checks
# it exists and carries no `params` block.
nextflow_config: nextflow.slurm.config

# The -profile the generated submit body passes to nextflow. A container runtime is a
# property of the venue, not of the science: this cluster runs apptainer. A venue that
# supplies each process's container itself (AWS Batch) sets it to "" (quoted -- a bare
# empty value reads as a section opener in the narrow parser), meaning no -profile.
nextflow_profile: apptainer
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The workspace's batch executor, as a setting rather than a spelling (decision 0039).

GARS submits real work to a managed scheduler and never runs it in the current process
(decision 0027). That ruling is scheduler-agnostic; only its spelling was Slurm-coupled --
`sbatch` lived in generated bytes and in contract prose, so a site without Slurm could not
run GARS at all.

This module is the one door. It reads `_config/executor.yaml` from the project and answers
three questions:

    header(...)          the directives block a generated submit.sh opens with
    submit(script)       the argv that hands that script to the scheduler -> a job id
    status(job_id)       the argv that asks after it -> PENDING | RUNNING | COMPLETED | FAILED

No descriptor file, or `name: slurm`, means the built-in Slurm descriptor, whose bytes are
identical to what this system generated before the seam existed (pinned by a golden-bytes
test). A cluster that upgrades GARS notices nothing.

The built-in `local` backend runs the generated script under `nohup`-style detachment and
reports the PID as the job id. It exists so the deterministic core can exercise a real
submit -> status -> completion walk with no cluster at all; it is POSIX-only, like every
other assumption this system already makes, and it is NOT a venue for analyses -- stage 03's
venue gate is unchanged.

Runs on stock python 3.6.8, stdlib only, like every `_system/` helper.
"""

import argparse
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

EXIT_OK, EXIT_FAILURE, EXIT_REFUSED, EXIT_USAGE = 0, 1, 2, 3

#: The closed state vocabulary every backend maps onto. A caller polls until it sees a
#: terminal state; nothing else is a legal answer.
STATES = ("PENDING", "RUNNING", "COMPLETED", "FAILED")

#: The placeholders a `directives` line may name. Anything else is a descriptor error, said
#: by name rather than raised as a KeyError from inside a format string.
HEADER_FIELDS = ("project", "assay", "substage", "partition", "time", "cpus", "mem")

DESCRIPTOR_NAME = "executor.yaml"

#: Where the `local` backend keeps what it needs to answer `status` for a PID it started.
LOCAL_JOBS_DIR = ".gars_local_jobs"

SLURM = {
    "name": "slurm",
    "directives": [
        "#SBATCH --job-name={project}-{assay}",
        "#SBATCH --partition={partition}",
        "#SBATCH --time={time}",
        "#SBATCH --cpus-per-task={cpus}",
        "#SBATCH --mem={mem}",
        "#SBATCH --output={substage}/logs/slurm-%j.out",
        "#SBATCH --error={substage}/logs/slurm-%j.err",
    ],
    "submit_argv": ["sbatch", "{script}"],
    "job_id_regex": r"Submitted batch job (\d+)",
    "status_argv": ["sacct", "-j", "{job_id}", "--format=State", "--noheader"],
    "status_map": {
        "PENDING": "PENDING", "CONFIGURING": "PENDING", "REQUEUED": "PENDING",
        "SUSPENDED": "PENDING", "PREEMPTED": "PENDING",
        "RUNNING": "RUNNING", "COMPLETING": "RUNNING", "RESIZING": "RUNNING",
        "COMPLETED": "COMPLETED",
        "FAILED": "FAILED", "CANCELLED": "FAILED", "TIMEOUT": "FAILED",
        "NODE_FAIL": "FAILED", "OUT_OF_MEMORY": "FAILED", "BOOT_FAIL": "FAILED",
        "DEADLINE": "FAILED", "REVOKED": "FAILED",
    },
    "nextflow_config": "nextflow.slurm.config",
    #: The -profile the generated submit body passes to nextflow. A container runtime is a
    #: property of the venue, not of the science: this cluster runs apptainer; AWS Batch
    #: supplies each process's container itself and wants no profile at all (empty = omit).
    "nextflow_profile": "apptainer",
    "submit_note": "Slurm snapshots this script at submission: editing it never affects a "
                   "queued job.",
}

LOCAL = {
    "name": "local",
    "directives": [
        "# Executor: local. No scheduler directives -- this script is run directly, detached.",
        "# compute.* stays in the record: partition={partition} time={time} "
        "cpus={cpus} mem={mem}",
    ],
    "submit_argv": [],          # the local backend submits in-process, not through an argv
    "job_id_regex": "",
    "status_argv": [],
    "status_map": {},
    "nextflow_config": "",
    "nextflow_profile": "",
    "submit_note": "This script is run directly on this machine; editing it mid-run is a "
                   "race you will lose.",
}

BUILTINS = {"slurm": SLURM, "local": LOCAL}


# --- the descriptor ----------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _strip_value(raw):
    """A scalar: quoted span taken whole, otherwise up to an inline ` #` comment.

    Quoted first, deliberately: a Slurm directive line IS a comment (`#SBATCH ...`), so a
    naive comment strip would eat the descriptor's most important content.
    """
    raw = raw.strip()
    if raw[:1] in ('"', "'"):
        quote = raw[0]
        end = raw.find(quote, 1)
        if end != -1:
            return raw[1:end]
        return raw[1:]
    return re.split(r"\s+#", raw, maxsplit=1)[0].strip()


def parse_descriptor(text):
    """The narrow parser for a template we own -- scalars, one-level lists, one-level maps.

    The same trade `wrapperlib.read_config` makes (decision 0011): stdlib-only means no YAML
    library, and the template's shape is fixed and documented in the template itself.
    """
    values = {}
    section = None
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        if not raw.strip() or raw.lstrip().startswith("#"):
            continue
        m = re.match(r"^([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*):\s*(.*)$", raw)
        if m:
            key, rest = m.group(1), m.group(2)
            if rest.strip():
                values[key] = _strip_value(rest)
                section = None
            else:
                section = key
                values[key] = None      # shape decided by the first child line
            continue
        m = re.match(r"^\s+-\s+(.*)$", raw)
        if m and section:
            if not isinstance(values.get(section), list):
                values[section] = []
            values[section].append(_strip_value(m.group(1)))
            continue
        m = re.match(r"^\s+([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*):\s*(.*)$", raw)
        if m and section:
            if not isinstance(values.get(section), dict):
                values[section] = {}
            values[section][m.group(1)] = _strip_value(m.group(2))
            continue
    return values


def descriptor_path(config_root):
    return Path(config_root) / "_config" / DESCRIPTOR_NAME


def load(config_root):
    """The descriptor for a project. Absent file -> the built-in Slurm descriptor.

    `config_root` is the directory that owns `_config/` -- the project, in GARS's layout.
    """
    path = descriptor_path(config_root)
    if not path.is_file():
        return dict(SLURM)
    parsed = parse_descriptor(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    name = parsed.get("name") or "slurm"
    base = dict(BUILTINS.get(name, {"name": name}))
    for key, value in parsed.items():
        if value is not None:
            base[key] = value
    base.setdefault("name", name)
    return base


def validate(descriptor):
    """Problems with a descriptor, in member words. Empty list means usable."""
    problems = []
    name = descriptor.get("name")
    if not name:
        problems.append("the descriptor has no `name:` line; name the backend "
                        "(slurm, local, or your own)")
    directives = descriptor.get("directives")
    if directives is not None and not isinstance(directives, list):
        problems.append("`directives:` must be a list of `- \"...\"` lines")
    elif isinstance(directives, list):
        for line in directives:
            for field in re.findall(r"\{([A-Za-z_]+)\}", line):
                if field not in HEADER_FIELDS:
                    problems.append("directive line names {%s}, which this system does not "
                                    "supply; available: %s"
                                    % (field, ", ".join("{%s}" % f for f in HEADER_FIELDS)))
    if name not in BUILTINS:
        submit_argv = descriptor.get("submit_argv")
        if not isinstance(submit_argv, list) or not submit_argv:
            problems.append("`submit_argv:` must be a non-empty list; it runs the GENERATED "
                            "script and nothing else")
        elif not any("{script}" in a for a in submit_argv):
            problems.append("`submit_argv:` never names {script}; the generated submit.sh is "
                            "the only thing a descriptor may submit")
        status_argv = descriptor.get("status_argv")
        if not isinstance(status_argv, list) or not status_argv:
            problems.append("`status_argv:` must be a non-empty list naming {job_id}")
        elif not any("{job_id}" in a for a in status_argv):
            problems.append("`status_argv:` never names {job_id}")
        if not descriptor.get("job_id_regex"):
            problems.append("`job_id_regex:` is required: it is how the submit output "
                            "becomes a job id")
        else:
            try:
                re.compile(descriptor["job_id_regex"])
            except re.error as exc:
                problems.append("`job_id_regex:` does not compile (%s) -- remember the "
                                "parser takes a quoted value verbatim, with no escape "
                                "processing; a regex needing a double quote must be "
                                "single-quoted" % exc)
        status_map = descriptor.get("status_map")
        if not isinstance(status_map, dict) or not status_map:
            problems.append("`status_map:` must map this backend's states onto %s"
                            % "|".join(STATES))
        else:
            unknown = sorted({v for v in status_map.values() if v not in STATES})
            if unknown:
                problems.append("`status_map:` maps onto %s, which are not in the closed "
                                "vocabulary %s" % (", ".join(unknown), "|".join(STATES)))
    return problems


# --- the three doors ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _fill(text, fields):
    """Substitute the KNOWN {tokens} and leave every other brace alone.

    Deliberately not str.format: a descriptor element may legitimately contain literal

usage: executorlib.py submit [-h] [--workspace WORKSPACE] script

positional arguments:
  script

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --workspace WORKSPACE
                        the project directory that owns _config/

#"'!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Compute and plot PCA of the planned RNA-seq gene counts."""
import argparse
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--counts", required=True, type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--design", required=True, type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--outdir", required=True, type=Path)
    args = parser.parse_args()

    design = pd.read_csv(args.design)
    required = {"sample_id", "condition"}
    if not required.issubset(design.columns):
        raise ValueError("Design must contain sample_id and condition columns")
    if design.sample_id.duplicated().any():
        raise ValueError("Design contains duplicate sample IDs")

    counts = pd.read_csv(args.counts, sep="'"\\t\")
    if \"gene_id\" not in counts.columns:
        raise ValueError(\"Gene counts table has no gene_id column\")
    sample_ids = design.sample_id.astype(str).tolist()
    if set(sample_ids) "'!= set(counts.columns) & set(sample_ids) or not set(sample_ids).issubset(counts.columns):
        raise ValueError("Count table sample columns do not match the six design sample IDs")
    values = counts[sample_ids].apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    if values.isna().any().any() or not np.isfinite(values.to_numpy()).all():
        raise ValueError("Gene count sample columns contain non-numeric or non-finite values")
    if (values < 0).any().any():
        raise ValueError("Gene counts contain negative values")

    library_totals = values.sum(axis=0)
    if (library_totals <= 0).any():
        raise ValueError("At least one sample has a zero library total")
    cpm = values.div(library_totals, axis=1) * 1_000_000
    keep = (cpm >= 1).sum(axis=1) >= 3
    if keep.sum() < 2:
        raise ValueError("Fewer than two genes pass CPM >= 1 in at least three samples")
    transformed = np.log2(cpm.loc[keep] + 1).T
    scaled = StandardScaler().fit_transform(transformed)
    pca = PCA(n_components=2)
    coordinates = pca.fit_transform(scaled)

    scores = pd.DataFrame({
        "sample_id": sample_ids,
        "condition": design.condition.astype(str).tolist(),
        "PC1": coordinates[:, 0],
        "PC2": coordinates[:, 1],
    })
    args.outdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    scores.to_csv(args.outdir / "sample_pca_scores.csv", index=False)

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 5.5))
    palette = {condition: plt.get_cmap("tab10")(i) for i, condition in
               enumerate(dict.fromkeys(scores.condition))}
    for condition, group in scores.groupby("condition", sort=False):
        ax.scatter(group.PC1, group.PC2, label=condition, color=palette[condition], s=75)
        for _, row in group.iterrows():
            ax.annotate(row.sample_id, (row.PC1, row.PC2), xytext=(5, 5),
                        textcoords="offset points", fontsize=9)
    ax.set_xlabel("PC1 ({:.1f}% variance)".format(pca.explained_variance_ratio_[0] * 100))
    ax.set_ylabel("PC2 ({:.1f}% variance)".format(pca.explained_variance_ratio_[1] * 100))
    ax.set_title("RNA-seq sample PCA")
    ax.legend(title="Condition")
    ax.axhline(0, color="0.85", linewidth=0.7, zorder=0)
    ax.axvline(0, color="0.85", linewidth=0.7, zorder=0)
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(args.outdir / "sample_pca.png", dpi=200)
    plt.close(fig)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
